Player A casts a Tempting Wurm. As the trigger resolves, Player B chooses to put a Venarian Gold onto the battlefield, attached to the Tempting Wurm. What happens?

The value of X as Player B cast Venarian Gold is undefined, so Player B puts no sleep counters on Tempting Wurm. (107.2) Player B will tap the Tempting Wurm, but it will untap normally during its controller's future untap steps.

key_points: no sleep counters are put on Tempting Wurm, because X is 0 for a permanent that was never cast
Tempting Wurm is still tapped by Venarian Gold's effect
Tempting Wurm untaps normally during its controller's future untap steps
common_errors: claiming the Wurm stays tapped indefinitely
putting some nonzero number of sleep counters on it

messages.content: You are a Magic: The Gathering rules expert. Answer precisely and cite comprehensive rule numbers.

Player A and Player B each control a Death's Shadow. Player A has 6 life and Player B has 9. Player A attacks with their Death's Shadow, and Player B blocks it with theirs. Player A casts Temur Battle Rage targeting their Death's Shadow. If Player B is dealt as much damage as possible during combat, what is their resulting life total?

1. In the first combat damage step, Player A can assign 6 damage to Player B's Death's Shadow and 1 damage to Player B. (702.19b) Player B's Death's Shadow will die before the second combat damage step (510.3, 704.3, 510.4), at which point Player B will be dealt another 7 damage. (702.19d)

Assigning any other amount of damage to Death's Shadow in the first combat damage step would result in less total damage dealt to Player B. In particular, assigning any less than 6 damage to Player B's Death's Shadow in the first combat damage step will result in it surviving and being able to block more damage in the second combat damage step.

key_points: Player B ends at 1 life
in the first-strike damage step Player A assigns 6 damage to the blocking Death's Shadow and 1 to Player B
the blocker dies before the regular combat damage step, so all 7 damage is dealt to Player B then
common_errors: arriving at a final life total other than 1
assigning less than lethal damage to the blocker so it survives to absorb damage twice
